newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P assigns Bpi to Toho Mutual Life, two others.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns Bpi to Toho Mutual Life, two others.

text.p: Standard & Poor's Corp (S&P) said on Wednesday that it had assigned a Bpi rating to Toho Mutual Life Insurance Co and two other Japanese life insurers.
The other two insurers are Kyoei Life Insurance Co Ltd and Nippon Dantai Life Insurance Co Ltd.
S&P also said it had assigned a BBBpi rating to Taiyo Mutual Life Insurance Co and an A+ CPA rating to Daido Mutual Life Insurance Co Ltd.
A CPA rating is a claims-paying ability rating based partly on information available only from company management, S&P said.
A pi rating is based on an analysis of an insurer's published financial information as well as other public information, S&P said.
S&P said it had affirmed a Bpi rating of Chiyoda Mutual Life Insurance Co and a BBpi rating of Mitsui Mutual Life Insurance Co.
It also affirmed BBBpi ratings of Asahi Mutual Life Insurance Co and Sumitomo Life Insurance Co and an Api rating of Dai-ichi Mutual Life Insurance Co.
S&P also affirmed an AA- CPA rating of Meiji Life Insurance Co and an AA+ CPA rating of Nippon Life Insurance Co.
It also affirmed A+ of Yasuda Mutual Life Insurance Co.

S&P said that, while the life insurance industry received a much-needed respite in the year to March 31, 1997 as negative spreads on investment products eased, it faces the challenges of new players entering the market and increasingly selective policyholders.
It said that these factors will test the resilience of the companies' business franchises and will have a profound impact on how participants structure and deliver their products.
"Differentiation among life insurers in terms of financial strength is likely to widen as their strategies are tested," it said.

In the near term, S&P expects the life insurers will have a chance to catch their breath as assumed interest rates on corporate pensions have been lowered retrospectively and those on new insurance policies sold to retail clients will likely come down further, reducing the burden of negative spreads between product yields and investment returns.
In the long term, profitability is expected to come under further pressure as mortality-factor profits are squeezed by increasing competition, S&P said.
Insurers also will need to improve their cost structures in order to stay competitive, it said.
As the operating environment changes, some factors are seen as critical for success in the industry, S&P said.

These include strong capitalisation, strong portfolio management and prudent asset-liability management, strong business franchises with efficient, market-focused, multichannel distribution systems, and cost effectiveness, S&P said.
Meanwhile, the volatile Nikkei stock sverage will continue to cloud the industry's financial flexibility and capital position, it said.
